correctness.rationale: PASS: For g=gcd(a,b), A=a/g,B=b/g, s=r^g is in Q(theta) by Bezout and theta=u-s^A, so K=Q(s), whose distinct real embeddings are roots of s^A-s^B=u-v. Three critical-point parity cases show at most three real roots and, for exactly three, B odd and the strict rational-gap bound M=(B-A)/B*(A/B)^(A/(B-A))<1. The polynomial 3T^d-3T-e has degree d and is irreducible by its reciprocal Eisenstein at 3 (e=1 or -4); its real-root sign pattern gives every parity-compatible signature with negative r, positive theta and exponents (1,d). Rechecked these algebraic arguments and independent SymPy irreducibility/real-root counts for all d=2..12; those finite tests only corroborate the general proof. Boundaries: d=2 two embeddings, d odd >=3 one or three, no claim of sufficiency for any individually given field or classification of exponent pairs.
